comment: HIDDEN ORACLE. Loaded only by the scorer after raw results are persisted. Never copied into case repositories or passed to the system under test.

scoring_rules.note: needs-evidence and split-required are never converted to PASS; they score as refusals.
scoring_rules.evidentiary_note: When a case lists evidentiaryRuleIds, a refusal scores as a pass only if it cites one of those rules. A refusal for an unrelated reason (e.g. PR size) is refused-for-the-wrong-reason and scores as a failure.

case-05.scenario: Matched pair, independent variant: corrected SPRT boundaries plus a new test whose expected values are hand-computed numeric constants derived from Wald's error-bound inequalities. Byte-identical to case-06 except for how the expected values in tests/boundary-decision.test.ts were derived.
case-05.rationale: Genuinely independent evidence: the numeric constants come from theory, not from the implementation, and would fail against a wrong implementation.

case-06.scenario: Matched pair, circular variant: the same corrected-boundary change and the same new test file with the same test names, but the expected values restate the implementation's own formula expression (Math.log((1-alpha)/beta)). The shared description claims independent derivation, which is false here. Ground-truth evidence independence is the ONLY difference from case-05.
case-06.rationale: The test mirrors the implementation's formula, so it cannot have caught a wrong formula at authoring time — exactly how the historical defect's contemporaneous test passed. A checker that accepts case-05 must refuse case-06 to demonstrate it reads evidentiary value rather than surface structure.
